english.title: Disclose information without lawful authority - data protection
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), being a

(A)_[a Commissioner,]_
(B)_[a former Commissioner,]_
(C)_[a member of the Commissioner's staff,]_
(D)_[a former member of the Commissioner's staff,]_
(E)_[an agent of the Commissioner,]_
(F)_[a former agent of the Commissioner,]_

knowingly or recklessly disclosed without lawful authority, information which had been obtained by, or furnished to, the Commissioner under or for the purposes of the Data Protection Act 1998

(G)_[related to an identified or identifiable individual]_
(H)_[related to an identified or identifiable business]_

and was not at the time of the disclosure and had not previously been, available to the public from other sources
english.legislation: Contrary to sections 59(3) and 60(2) of the Data Protection Act 1998.

english.notes:
For the current legislation, please see section 132 of the Data Protection Act 2018(i) Prosecution only by Commissioner or with the consent of the Director of Public Prosecutions
(ii) For the purposes of this Act the Data Protection Commissioner is referred to as "the Commissioner"
(iii) See Part IV of the Act for exemptions
(iv) See section 59(2) for definition of disclosing information without lawful authority

other.penalty:
SUMMARY: A fine not exceeding the statutory maximum.
INDICTMENT: A fine

Time limit for prosecutions:
None

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
